important.name: README claims rule T2 flags every stale snapshot page, but T2 hashes only id, rank, status and title of the top-N rows
important.summary:
README.md:410-412 says a bare `add --spec`, `retire`, `split`, `refresh` or `migrate-ids` leaves the page as it was "and rule T2 flags it until then" (the snapshot_html.py module docstring at lines 5-6 repeats it). T2 (rules_todo.py:78-94) compares the header against `rows_sha256` (sources.py:131-135), which hashes only `[id, rank, status, title]` of the first top_n items. The new page draws far more than that: the Summary block counts the whole catalog (items, per status, per kind, trackers, close candidates) and each row shows kind, blast, LoE, score, GH issues and the folded prose. So a `retire` of an item outside the top N, or an edit to a top item's kind, score, gh_issues, summary or proposed change, leaves a stale page with T2 clean. A reader relying on the documented contract would trust a page that T2 never flags.

Also (system_shape): README.md:411-412 says a bare `add --spec`, `retire`, `split`, `refresh` or `migrate-ids` leaves the page as it was "and rule T2 flags it until then"; snapshot_html.py:5-6 makes the same claim. T2 compares only the header `rows_sha256`, and `rows_sha256` (sources.py:131-135) hashes `[id, rank, status, title]` of the first top_n items. The page this PR adds draws much more than that: the Summary block counts the whole catalog (items, status and kind counts, trackers, close candidates; snapshot_html.py:196-209), and each row shows kind, blast, LoE, score, GH links and the folded prose (snapshot_html.py:140-175). So `add --spec` or `retire` of an item below the top N, a `refresh` that rescores without reranking, or an edit to a top item's summary or kind leaves the page out of date while T2 stays clean. Before this PR the same gap existed for the table's extra columns, but the docs did not claim otherwise, and the new Summary block widens it to any catalog write.

Also (docs): README.md:413 (168 columns) and 414 (123) and docs/RELEASES/v1.0.0.md:187 (166) were not rewrapped after an insertion, so they stand out from the ~110-column paragraphs around them and make the raw-text diff harder to read.

Also (overall): README.md:413-414 (the snapshot page paragraph: `summary of the catalog (item count, ...`, `GitHub issues), with each item's summary, ...`) and docs/RELEASES/v1.0.0.md:187 (`retire`, `split`, ... `The page holds a Summary block ...`) run to 123-168 characters, while every neighbouring line wraps near 115. Rendering is unaffected; the raw files read unevenly and the diffs of later edits get noisy.

Also (runtime, adv_code_runtime): snapshot_html.py:4-6 says a bare add --spec, retire, split, refresh or migrate-ids 'leaves the page for the next render, which rule T2 flags until then'. T2 (rules_todo.py:91) compares only rows_sha256, the hash of [id, rank, status, title] of the top-N rows (sources.py:131-135). The new page also draws a whole-catalog Summary block (item count, status and kind counts, trackers, close candidates; snapshot_html.py:196-209) and per-row kind, blast, LoE, score, GH and folded prose, none of which feed the hash. Adding or retiring an item ranked below top-N, a refresh that changes scores without reordering, or a prose/kind/issue edit leaves the page stale (wrong Items count, wrong scores) while T2 reports no drift, contradicting the stated contract.

Also (adv_code_runtime): The module docstring says a bare `add --spec`, `retire`, `split`, `refresh` or `migrate-ids` leaves the page for the next render, "which rule T2 flags until then". T2 compares only `rows_sha256`, the hash of `[id, rank, status, title]` for the top-N rows (plugins/harness/lib/harness_lib/todo_sync/sources.py:131-135). The new page also draws a whole-catalog Summary (item count, status and kind counts, trackers, close candidates; snapshot_html.py:196-209) and, for each top row, kind, score, GH and folded prose. Adding or retiring an item below the top N, changing a non-top item's status, or a `refresh` that rescores without reordering changes the page but not the hash, so T2 reports the stale page as current.

Attack: Probe docs/_scratch/pr_review/0300/pr300_20261117T144102Z/probes/t2_stale.py, top_n=1. Before: items T-1 (rank 1, open, kind bug, score 1.0) and T-2 (rank 2, open). After: T-1 changes to kind feature, score 9.0 and gets a summary; T-2 becomes done; T-3 (rank 3) is added; trackers=[1]. Output: `hash equal: True`, `summary equal: False`, `top row equal: False`. End to end: render, then append a rank-99 item to RepoToDo.json (what `add --spec` does) or set a non-top item's status to done (what `retire` does), then run `todo_sync.py check --rules T2`. No T2 finding appears, yet TODO_Snapshot.html still shows the old Items/Status/Kind counts.
fix: Narrow the prose in README.md:411-412 and snapshot_html.py:5-6 to what T2 checks, e.g. "... leaves the page as it was until the next render; rule T2 flags it when the top-N ids, ranks, statuses or titles changed (the Summary counts, the other columns and the folded prose are not checked)".

Widen the T2 hash so it covers what the page draws (top-N row fields plus the Summary counts), keeping README and docstring as written; this changes every existing header hash, so the first check after the upgrade warns until a render.

Narrow the claim in README.md:411-412 and snapshot_html.py:5-6 to what T2 checks, e.g. "rule T2 flags it when the top-N ids, ranks, statuses or titles changed; other edits (counts, scores, prose) show after the next render".

Or widen the drift check so it matches the page: hash what the page draws (the top-N rows' displayed fields plus the Summary counts), and update the T2 docstring (rules_todo.py t2_snapshot), the `rows_sha256` docstring and the header format note to match.
Rewrap README.md:412-415 and docs/RELEASES/v1.0.0.md:186-193 at 110 columns with the same text.
Rewrap README.md:410-416 and docs/RELEASES/v1.0.0.md:184-193 to the width the surrounding paragraphs use.

Narrow the docstring at snapshot_html.py:4-6 (and the matching sentence in the page intro or skill docs if repeated) to say T2 flags only a change to the top-N rows' id, rank, status or title, and that Summary counts and other columns can go stale silently until the next render.

Or widen the freshness check: add a second header field (for example a sha256 over the catalog fields the page draws, including the Summary counts) written by snapshot_header and compared by t2_snapshot, keeping rows_sha256 for D10.

Make the header hash cover what the page draws: hash the Summary inputs (all items' id/status/kind plus the trackers and close_candidates sizes) and the drawn fields of the top rows, and have T2 compare that.
Correct the docstring at snapshot_html.py:5-6 to say T2 flags only a change to the top-N id, rank, status or title, and that the Summary and the other cells can go stale with no finding.

important.name: New %, # and ? href encoding in link_target has no test
important.summary:
The PR adds "%" -> %25, "#" -> %23 and "?" -> %3F to stub_links._ENCODE so a stub path on the HTML page never becomes a fragment, a query or a bad escape, but no test in the suite asserts any of the three. tests/lib/test_todo_sync_stub_links.py:149-154 still checks only space, parentheses, <> and |, and the new page tests use plain Alpha/Beta paths. Reverting the map leaves the whole suite green, so a stub folder named e.g. `C#` or `What?` would link to the wrong target with nothing to catch it.

Also (overall): stub_links.py now percent-encodes `%`, `#` and `?` in snapshot hrefs, and its docstring promises that an existing `%` never double-encodes an escape the function adds. No test under tests/ exercises any of the three characters (no `%25`, `%23` or `%3F` anywhere); test_link_target at tests/lib/test_todo_sync_stub_links.py:149-152 covers only space and parentheses. Dropping a map entry, or a reordered two-pass encode that double-encodes, would still pass every test.

Attack: Probe at the PR head: a pytest plugin (probes/patch_encode.py) resets stub_links._ENCODE to the pre-PR map {' ': '%20', '(': '%28', ')': '%29', '<': '%3C', '>': '%3E', '|': '%7C'}. Running `PYTHONPATH=<probes> hpy -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider -p patch_encode tests/lib/test_todo_sync_stub_links.py tests/lib/test_todo_snapshot_html.py tests/lib/test_todo_snapshot_wiring.py` gives 53 passed. Grep over tests/ for %23, %3F or %25 finds nothing. With the old map, link_target("docs/RESEARCH/C#/_IMPL_TODO.md", "docs/RESEARCH/_TODO/Snapshots") returns "../../C#/_IMPL_TODO.md", which a browser resolves to ../../C plus a fragment, and no test fails.

Also (system_shape): stub_links.py:17-18 adds `%`, `#` and `?` to `_ENCODE`, and the link_target docstring (stub_links.py:110-118) promises a path never turns into a fragment, query or bad escape and that an existing `%` never double-encodes. test_todo_sync_stub_links.py:149-154 still checks only space, parentheses, `<>` and `|`, so dropping any of the three new entries would leave every test green.
fix: Extend test_link_target in tests/lib/test_todo_sync_stub_links.py with a stub path holding %, # and ? (e.g. "docs/RESEARCH/C#1 50%?/_IMPL_TODO.md" -> "../../C%231%2050%25%3F/_IMPL_TODO.md"), checking that each character is encoded once and that an existing %20 in the path becomes %2520
Add a render_page case in tests/lib/test_todo_snapshot_html.py or tests/scripts/test_todo_sync_render_page.py whose stub folder name holds # or ?, and assert that the href carries %23 / %3F

Add a case to tests/lib/test_todo_sync_stub_links.py::test_link_target (or a new test beside it) asserting link_target("docs/R/a%b#c?d/_IMPL_TODO.md", SNAP_DIR) ends with "a%25b%23c%3Fd/_IMPL_TODO.md", which pins all three encodings and the single-pass rule.
Add an assertion to test_link_target, e.g. `link_target("docs/RESEARCH/a%20#b?c/_IMPL_TODO.md", SNAP_DIR) == "../../a%2520%23b%3Fc/_IMPL_TODO.md"`.

minor.name: todo.gh.repo row implies render calls gh when the key is set
minor.summary:
README.md:543 says "with `null`, `render` makes no `gh` call: only an item's `gh_issue` source url links, otherwise the item shows plain `#N`". The contrast implies `render` calls `gh` when a repo is set, but render never runs `gh`: `render_snapshot` passes `todo.gh_repo` straight into `SnapshotPage`, and `snapshot_html._issue_url` (lines 108-118) builds `https://github.com/<repo>/issues/<N>` from the string. The Default column (`null` = the repository `gh` resolves for the checkout) holds for `untracked` and `--file-issue`, not for render, which with `null` resolves nothing.

Also (system_shape): README.md:543 says "with `null`, `render` makes no `gh` call". render never calls `gh`: with a repo set it only builds `https://github.com/<repo>/issues/N` strings (snapshot_html.py:108-118). The parenthetical suggests a non-null repo makes render reach the network, which the page's no-network design (snapshot_html.py:9-10) rules out.
fix: Reword the render clause in README.md:543 to: "`todo_sync.py render` links issues on the snapshot page without calling `gh`: an item's `gh_issue` source url first, else `https://github.com/<repo>/issues/N` from this key; with `null`, an issue without a source url shows plain `#N`".

Replace the parenthetical with: "render builds `https://github.com/<repo>/issues/N` links without calling `gh`; with `null` only an item's `gh_issue` source url links, otherwise the item shows plain `#N`".

minor.name: todo.gh.repo description still says the issue fetch is not built
minor.summary:
The rewritten todo.gh.repo description ends with 'Phase 3: the fetch is not built yet, so no rule reads it today'. The key is read by code outside render: issues.py passes cfg.todo.gh_repo as --repo to the gh issue list call (line 108, `todo_sync.py untracked`) and to file_issue (line 156, `add --file-issue`). The same sentence also says render reads it, so the text contradicts itself and the code. The PR rewrote this description and carried the stale clause over.

Also (system_shape): This PR rewrote the `todo.gh.repo` description (harness.schema.json:202) and kept its old tail: "by the issue fetch, where null means the origin remote (Phase 3: the fetch is not built yet, so no rule reads it today)". The README key row (README.md:543) and the `untracked` docstring in scripts/todo_sync.py say `todo_sync.py untracked`, `add --file-issue` and `inbox put --file-issue` read the key today, and that null means the repository `gh` resolves for the checkout, not the origin remote. The schema now names render as a reader but still says nothing else reads it.
fix: Reword the tail of the description to name its readers: render (issue links), `todo_sync.py untracked` and `add --file-issue` (the --repo given to gh); null: render builds no link, and gh resolves the repository from the origin remote. Drop the 'Phase 3 ... not built yet' clause.

Rewrite the schema description to match the README row: read by render (issue links on the snapshot page), `todo_sync.py untracked`, `add --file-issue` and `inbox put --file-issue`; null: the repository `gh` resolves for the checkout (render then links only from an item's gh_issue source url).

But neither the TASK-2 receipt deviations nor DesignEvolution.json records the departure, so the plan and the code disagree with no explanation.

Alternatively, add a one-line comment above TODO_OUTPUTS in tests/contract/test_root_separation.py giving that reason, so the departure from the plan is visible at the test.

minor.name: Loader reload behavior is pinned by regex over JS source, not by running it
minor.summary: test_the_loader_reloads_only_on_a_new_stamp (tests/lib/test_todo_snapshot_html.py:244-251) asserts the reload guard through LIVE_GUARD and RELOAD_ONCE regexes and call counts in todo.js text. That is a structural check, not behavior: a whitespace or variable-shape change breaks it with no change in behavior, and a semantically wrong guard written in a different textual shape (e.g. `!=` against a coerced value, or a guard moved into a helper) would fail it, while some broken variants matching the textual shape would pass. Not a mock chain, but it is the only coverage of the live-reload contract.
fix: Keep the regex test as a smoke check and add a behavioral test that runs todo.js under a tiny JS harness (node with stubbed window, document, sessionStorage and location.reload), asserting: no reload on equal stamp, one reload on a new stamp, no second reload for the same stamp.
If no JS runtime is acceptable in the Python suite, document in the test docstring that it is a structural guard and name where the behavior is exercised manually.

minor.name: New OSError branch in init's snapshot step has no test
minor.summary:
scaffold._first_snapshot now catches (TodoSyncError, OSError) and rewraps both as a TodoSyncError naming the catalog left behind (an OSError can now come from reading the inlined pages/ assets or writing todo_live.js).
